newsitem.title: USA: TRADE MIXED ON CBOT DECISION TO DROP DAP CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: TRADE MIXED ON CBOT DECISION TO DROP DAP CONTRACT.

text.p: Most traders and industry consultants agree that the the Chicago Board of Trade's decision to delist its fertilizer contracts will have no impact on cash markets, but some traders lament the loss of a hedging instrument.
"It (delisting the contracts) was long overdue," said John Douglas, a consultant with Douglas and Associates in Florence, Ala. "Very few people used it."

Citing low volume, the CBOT Board of Directors voted in July to delist its anhydrous ammonia and diammonium phosphate contracts. The DAP contract was launched in October 1991, and the ammonia contract was launched in September 1992.
Record volume for the DAP contract was a scant 1,202 contracts reached in December 1992, and record volume for ammonia was 722 contracts, according to data from the CBOT.
Douglas said producers never used the contracts to hedge inventories, and most trade in the contracts was speculative.
"It was used as a gambling tool by only a few," he said.
However, some others in the trade said the fertilizer contracts were a valuble tool that should have been used more frequently.

"It's unfortunate that the industry didn't accept it," said one DAP trader in the northeast. "A lot of the people that actually used the product are also grain handlers that have been hedging in the grain markets forever."
The trader said she initially used the DAP contract to hedge her inventory, but stopped because the market became so illiquid that she often got stuck in trades.
The delisting of the contract will not have any impact on fertilizer markets or prices, market observers said.
"The industry generally had shunned it from the beginning," said Ed Wheeler, consultant with Wheeler and Associates in Washington, D.C. "It was having no impact on price."

The CBOT has not yet delisted the DAP and ammonia contracts because the exchange is waiting for the Commodities Futures Trading Commission to respond to its request, a spokesman for the exchange said.
